scenarios.name: n8n unavailable then real webhook fallback
new process recovers persisted post-n8n state

limits: Runtime delays were reduced to zero only in the test process; this run proves ordering and state transitions, not the 155-second wall-clock schedule.
SMTP was not used because no controlled SMTP server was configured; the real fallback receiver was an HTTP webhook.
Delivery is at-least-once across a crash after external acceptance and before the local success commit. Controlled receivers deduplicate by stable notification_id.
Single backend instance is assumed; distributed worker claiming is outside the approved architecture.
